I've many wondrous items that I think you'll appreciate, shopkeep," he replied. Possibly a very sad one." "It was a dragon." "It was a Clydesdale. Ten coppers." "Ten? I fought for this!" "You fought a Clydesdale." But she sighed and added, "Fine. Twelve, because you've never lied to me about the little things." Brakka squinted. "That's a compliment, right?" The traveler lay his sack down upon the countertop with a heavy *thump*, accompanied by the scrape of metal-on-metal, and unfurled the sack with a little flourish. Before it could be settled, the bell rang again. A slim elf in a velvet cloak slid in and set a small ring on the counter, the way a magician sets down a card. "Ring of Boundless Fortune. He set his hand upon the item furthest to his left and grinned. I'm told it's cursed, but only mildly." Odalys put on a second pair of glasses over her first pair. "This is the Razor Barb of Org-lak the Slayer, a mighty orc chieftain in the Higher Steppes. She turned the ring, watched the stone glow, and watched her own hand begin to itch. "Mildly?" "You may experience a streak of bad luck. Brief." "How brief?" "Weeks. Possibly seasons." "Forty gold." It has claimed the lives of many brave warriors, and is imbued with arcane magic, so as never to lose its edge!"" Marvelous!" I cried. "It's worth four hundred!" "It's worth four hundred to someone who hates me," Odalys said. "Which, to be fair, is a long list. Sixty. And you will tell nobody I bought it." "Five gold pieces!" The traveler's face fell, and his jubilance was overcome by a brief look of incredulity. The elf considered. He cleared his throat, and move on to the next piece." Perhaps this shall strike your fancy, then: the helmet of Ser Roderic the Brave, the most legendary knight in Warrior-King Rothac's retinue! He glanced at the door, behind which, apparently, someone angry was waiting. "Sixty-five, and I'll leave through the back." "Deal." You see, here, the gash borne by the axe of Medathu the Reviled, Scourge of the Seven Planes - and these singe marks from Rothornix, the Black Dragon. They shook on it. It is enchanted, much like the blade, to bestow unbridled courage to any man or woman that so dons it!" "My goodness, what a find!" I marveled, agape." Yes - yes, for this one, *eight* gold pieces, I think!" The traveler furrowed his brow, and it was clear that he felt slighted. "Okay - okay, perhaps another piece, good sir," he declared, laying his hand upon a hand-mirror." The mirror of Princess Gwedelyn, fairest maiden in the kingdom! It is, perhaps, the most magically astounding artefact I've ever beheld with mine own eyes, shopkeep. Any man may look into its reflection and see before him the spirit of Gwedelyn herself, fair and wise, and call upon her favor at a moment's notice! You see, her lingering spirit has the power to -" "Say no more, friend!" I interrupted, beaming." *Three gold pieces* for this treasure!" The traveler slammed the mirror down on the countertop, nearly breaking it. Odalys dropped the ring into a lead-lined drawer marked DO NOT, and the drawer rattled in disagreement. Brakka, still lingering with twelve coppers in hand, cleared her throat.

text: July 17th 2265: In the woods the stories from a man's childhood take on new credibility. Once the trees close in and the sun light dances through the leaves the imagination runs wild. The air seems alive with magic. On a moonless night when the wind blows, each creak or snap or shuffle in the dark conjures up thoughts of lurking horrors every man hadn't thought of since boyhood. With every mile I become more convinced of our destination. I can see in my sister's face that she feels the same. **The Last Audit** We had always thought the stories our father had told us had been just that, stories. His great grandfathers, great grandfather the captain of the guard of a vault of treasure; the wealth of the planet's most powerful nation. Somewhere, deep beneath the ground in a land called Knox our ancestor had stood as chief protector of a treasure of pure gold vaster than imagination. Until one day they came and closed the vault, a new generation of guard was being introduced, all artificial, all intelligent. From the ridge, Fort Knox looked almost peaceful. Somehow, this didn't seem hard too believe while we grew up in the dark world dirty and hungry, always moving looking for food. Eighty years of kudzu had swallowed the barracks, and the old depository sat in the middle of it all like a gray tooth. Only the turrets spoiled the picture. In the two hundred and forty years since The Fall there had been many stories of great hordes of treasure from before, but nothing had been found, the before world was dead and gone. But somehow here in this jungle hope glimmers brightly. August 9th 2265: A jungle this dense could hold a thousand secrets safe from prying eyes. We’d have to practically trip over something too see it. If it weren’t for our map, a worn and faded page out of the great explorer Rand McNally's meticulously made Road Atlas, passed down through the generations we would never have made it this far. Only a week’s trek more, barring any unforeseen complications. August 12th 2265: Paul died of dysentery. Four of them stood on the corners of the fence, swinging in slow, patient arcs, and the dying sun flashed off their lenses each time they turned. August 16th 2265: Arrived at a clearing in the middle of the jungle. According to the map we should be directly at our destination though this can not be correct. It looks as though it is being maintained. There are no trees or weeds too be seen and in the center of the walled clearing the top of a large building is visible. I will send a few men over at first light as scouts. August 17th 2265: The scouts haven’t returned. August 18th 2265: Screams in the night. Horrible and long mixed with faint mechanical sighs. Marisol lowered her binoculars. "They're still running." They filled the whole jungle and in the dark it was impossible to locate their origin. "Solar," Dutch whispered. He had been an electrician before the collapse, and he talked about circuits the way other people talked about God. Some of the men say they came from within the walls. "Panels on every roof, batteries in the bunkers. I don’t want to believe that and we can’t wait any longer. I’ve talked with my sister, if the scouts don’t return by morning we’ll arm up and be going over the wall. Nobody ever told the system to stop." Five of them had left Louisville with a legend: a vault of gold bars stacked like firewood, untouched, enough to buy a kingdom. The legend hadn't mentioned the sentry drones on the Bardstown road. It hadn't mentioned the stretch of wire where Pell and Okafor walked up to look at the gate and were cut in half by a machine that had never once been told the war was over. Three left now. Marisol, Dutch, and Teo, who was fifteen and hadn't spoken since the fence. "The optics are their weakness," Dutch said. "When the sun drops behind that ridge, the glare blinds the north-corner lens. Ninety seconds. Maybe less." "Maybe less?" "I never said it was a good plan."
